29 A source of coherent light is incident on two slits, P and Q, which are placed 80 mm apart. The
light has a single frequency of 1.5  1012
Hz. The light from the slits meets on a screen that is a
distance of 4.0 m from the slits. The screen is parallel to a line joining the slits.
4.0 m
screen
P
intensity sensor
80 mm
Q
not to scale
An intensity sensor is placed on the screen at the midpoint of the interference pattern such that
the intensity reading is a maximum. The intensity sensor is moved along the screen.
The sensor travels through two intensity minima, two intensity maxima and stops in the middle of
the third intensity minimum.
Which distance does the sensor move through?
A
4.0 mm
B
10 mm
C
25 mm
D
50 mm

hints: Start from the given frequency $1.5 \times 10^{12} \text{ Hz}$ and slit separation $80 \text{ mm}$: first find the wavelength using $c = f\lambda$.
Use $w = \lambda D/a$ with $D = 4.0 \text{ m}$ to get the distance on the screen between adjacent bright maxima.
Count half-fringe steps from the central maximum: maximum to minimum is $0.5w$, minimum to maximum is $0.5w$, so add the steps up to the middle of the third minimum.
walkthrough: Find the wavelength of the light. $\lambda = c/f = 3.0 \times 10^8 / 1.5 \times 10^{12} = 2.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}$.

Calculate the two-slit fringe spacing on the screen $4.0 \text{ m}$ away. Slit separation $a = 80 \text{ mm} = 0.080 \text{ m}$, so $w = \lambda D/a = (2.0 \times 10^{-4} \times 4.0)/0.080 = 0.010 \text{ m} = 10 \text{ mm}$.

Track the sensor position in units of $w$ starting at the central maximum where path difference is zero. Moving outward, maxima occur at $0, w, 2w$ and minima occur halfway between at $0.5w, 1.5w, 2.5w$.
The journey passes 1st minimum at $0.5w$, 1st maximum at $w$, 2nd minimum at $1.5w$, 2nd maximum at $2w$, then stops at 3rd minimum at $2.5w$.
Distance moved $= 2.5w = 2.5 \times 10 \text{ mm} = 25 \text{ mm}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: 4.0 mm is far too small. It confuses the 4.0 m slit to screen distance with the mm-scale fringe spacing on the screen.

B.explanation: 10 mm is one fringe spacing $w$. The sensor moves 2.5 fringe spacings from the central maximum to the centre of the third minimum.

C.explanation: Fringe spacing is $w = 10 \text{ mm}$ and the described travel is $2.5w = 25 \text{ mm}$ from the central maximum.

D.explanation: 50 mm would be $5w$. This counts each named minimum and maximum as a full fringe spacing instead of half-spacing steps.
